# Ishikawa diagram syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-ishikawa/grammar/ishikawa.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Ishikawa (fishbone) diagram syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `ishikawa`
and `ishikawa-beta` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this file
(DESIGN §4.4).

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; on a line with
`style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` / `#123;` entities read as
opaque text that no rule takes apart; and a line break appended. Keywords are matched without
regard to case.

**Lines.** The first line of text is the effect, on the header line or after it. Every later
line is a cause, nested by its indent (spaces and tabs count one column each) under the last
cause indented less. The first cause's indent is the baseline: a cause indented less than it is
a top-level cause. A line may not start with the keyword. A blank or comment line counts as a
line where one may start, so a line right after two of them in a row (or one right after the
header) is an error, as in mermaid@12.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

An Ishikawa diagram is the keyword, then its lines, each followed by a line break, a blank
line or the end. Blank and comment lines may come before the keyword.

```ebnf
diagram = [ SPACELINE { SPACELINE | NL } ] ISHIKAWA [ NL ] statement stop { statement stop } ;
```

```ebnf
stop = ( NL | EOF | SPACELINE ) { NL | EOF } ;
```

```ebnf
statement = SPACELIST [ Node ]
          | Node
          | SPACELINE ;
```

The effect (the first one) or a cause, by its indent.

```ebnf
Node @Node = TEXT ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`.

Every rule ignores case: a rule for `ab` also matches `AB` and `aB`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | SPACELINE | `\s*%%.*` |  | A `%%` comment v12's comment removal left (after the keyword, or a bare `%%` line), with the blanks and line breaks before it: a blank line. |
| INITIAL | ISHIKAWA | `ishikawa-beta\b` |  | `ishikawa-beta` or `ishikawa`: starts an Ishikawa (fishbone) diagram. Its first line is the effect, at the head of the fish; the indented lines after it are the causes, as bones off the spine. |
| INITIAL | ISHIKAWA | `ishikawa\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | SPACELINE | `[\s]+[\n]` |  | Blanks up to the last line break of their run: a blank line. |
| INITIAL | NL | `[\n]+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | SPACELIST | `[\s]+` |  | The indent before a cause: how deep it is in the tree. |
| INITIAL | TEXT | `[^\n]+` |  | The effect or a cause: the rest of the line, blanks around it dropped. `<br>` breaks it. |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
